This PR adds a comprehensive **ARCHITECTURE.md** document that provides detailed documentation of the FitCore project's system architecture, design patterns, and technical implementation.

## What's Added

### 📚 ARCHITECTURE.md Document

A complete architectural reference (1,161 lines) covering:

#### **System Architecture**
- **Monolithic Modular Architecture**: Detailed explanation of how the application uses modular Django apps as bounded contexts
- **Layered Architecture**: Four-layer design (Presentation, Business Logic, Data Access, Infrastructure)
- **Visual Diagrams**: 4 Mermaid diagrams illustrating system flow, database relationships, API request/response cycles, and payment processing

#### **Django Apps Documentation**
Complete documentation for all 8 Django apps with their responsibilities, models, and key features:
- **users**: User management and profile system with custom email-based authentication
- **authapp**: Extended authentication with JWT and OAuth (Google/Apple)
- **meal**: Comprehensive nutrition management with AI-generated and manual meal planning
- **workout**: Workout content management with video library and progress tracking
- **health**: Health metrics tracking with device integration support
- **payment**: Subscription and payment processing with Stripe integration
- **notification**: Multi-channel notification delivery system
- **adminapp**: Enhanced admin interface for content management

#### **Technical Deep Dives**
- **Database Architecture**: Entity relationships, schema design principles, and data model documentation
- **API Architecture**: RESTful design patterns, versioning strategy, and endpoint structure
- **Authentication & Authorization**: JWT token flow, OAuth integration, and permission system
- **External Services Integration**: OpenAI API, payment gateways, health data providers, media storage
- **Data Flow**: Step-by-step flows for user registration, meal plan generation, workout tracking, and payment processing
- **Security Architecture**: Multi-layer security with CSRF/XSS protection, token management, and best practices
- **Scalability & Performance**: Query optimization, caching strategies, horizontal scaling, and async processing plans

#### **Technology Stack**
Complete breakdown of:
- Backend frameworks (Django 5.2, DRF)
- Authentication tools (Simple JWT, django-allauth)
- Database (PostgreSQL)
- Payment processing (Stripe)
- AI integration (OpenAI API)
- Frontend (React Native - separate repo)
- Deployment tools and recommendations

#### **Future Roadmap**
- Migration path to microservices architecture
- Planned technical improvements (Redis caching, Celery, rate limiting)
- Feature enhancements (social features, community, wearable integration)

- Links to the [ERD diagram](./FitCore%20ERD%20.png) for visual database schema
- Provides architectural context for the implemented features

body:
The WPF ToolTip style does not define a default Foreground color, and so inherits the Foreground of its parent element. This can cause readability issues from implicit styles set on parents. This branch sets a default ToolTip Foreground color.

This branch also makes the ToolTip Background and Border properties accessible on ToolTip.

Here is a simple UI to compare ToolTip behavior in main vs in this branch.
```
<Window.Resources>
    <Style TargetType="Button">
        <Setter Property="Foreground" Value="White" />
        <Setter Property="Background" Value="#444444" />
    </Style>
</Window.Resources>
<StackPanel>
    <Button Content="Style Foreground and Background Only"
            ToolTip="This is a tooltip" />
    <Button Content="Manual Button Foreground and Background"
                Foreground="Yellow"
                Background="Black"
                ToolTip="This is another tooltip with a manual button foreground and background" />
    <Button Content="Manual Tooltip Foreground and Background">
        <Button.ToolTip>
            <ToolTip Foreground="LightGreen"
                     Background="Brown"
                     BorderBrush="Pink"
                     Content="This is a manual tooltip background brown, border pink, and foreground light green" />
        </Button.ToolTip>
    </Button>
</StackPanel>
```

CVE-2025-48432: Potential log injection via unescaped request path
==================================================================

Internal HTTP response logging used ``request.path`` directly, allowing control
characters (e.g. newlines or ANSI escape sequences) to be written unescaped
into logs. This could enable log injection or forgery, letting attackers
manipulate log appearance or structure, especially in logs processed by
external systems or viewed in terminals.

Although this does not directly impact Django's security model, it poses risks
when logs are consumed or interpreted by other tools. To fix this, the internal
``django.utils.log.log_response()`` function now escapes all positional
formatting arguments using a safe encoding.

Major TUI improvements including session management, incremental streaming UX, and critical OAuth token refresh bug fix.

## Key Features

### TUI Enhancements
- **Session Management**: Switch between chat sessions with full CRUD operations
- **Settings Screen**: Configure authentication providers and preferences
- **Model Picker**: Select models from different providers
- **Incremental Streaming**: Real-time UI updates for tool results during assistant turns

- Sessions endpoints: show, create, update (with apply=now support)

- **OAuth Token Refresh**: Preserve `id_token` during token refresh (fixes ChatGPT Personal mode crashes)
- **Streaming Adapter**: Ensure non-nil streaming_adapter passed to providers
- **Session Data**: Fresh session data when switching authentication providers

## Root Cause: OAuth Token Refresh Bug
Token refresh worker was not preserving `id_token` from existing credentials when refreshing OAuth tokens. ChatGPT Personal mode requires `id_token` to extract `chatgpt_account_id`, causing TUI sessions to crash after token refresh with `{:error, :missing_id_token}`.

**Fix**: Preserve `id_token` during OAuth token refresh (follows same pattern as `refresh_token` preservation). `id_token` is a JWT that doesn't need refreshing unlike `access_token`.

## Test Fixes (Real fixes, no test theater)
- Removed obsolete tests: SSE frames, ApiKeysLive, AnthropicDefaultTools, RemoteRuntimeServerTools
- Fixed SuppliedContext tests: filter seed data by `editor=="system"` instead of immutable flag
- Fixed OpenAIFrameTimeline test: use shared sandbox mode for spawned process DB access
- Fixed GeminiEdit test: add file existence assertion for better error messages

Created in collaboration with @Leo6Leo 

This fixes a bug where a dynamic plugin would use its own copy of `getConsoleRequestHeaders` function, in which case the code always returns `undefined`. Instead, calling this function should always return an object with relevant HTTP headers.

To verify the changes, modify `dynamic-demo-plugin/src/components/UtilityConsumer.tsx` file as follows:
- add the following import:
  ```ts
  // Do NOT use non-index import '@openshift-console/dynamic-plugin-sdk/lib/utils/fetch'
  import { getConsoleRequestHeaders } from '@openshift-console/dynamic-plugin-sdk';
  ```
- add the following code into `ConsoleFetchConsumer` component:
  ```ts
  const [data, setData] = React.useState();
  // new code below
  const consoleHeaders = getConsoleRequestHeaders();
  console.log('# consoleHeaders', consoleHeaders); // log to browser console
  ```
- run Console Bridge server with demo plugin enabled (demo plugin server should run on port 9001):
  ```sh
  ./bin/bridge -plugins console-demo-plugin=http://localhost:9001/ -i18n-namespaces=plugin__console-demo-plugin
  ```
- on Console page, expand nav menu section "Demo Plugin" and click on "Test Utilities"
- open browser dev tools and check that `# consoleHeaders` have been logged as expected

author: 0xshishigami
body:
## Changes done
- Fixed contract ABI field names by analyzing Across's actual implementation.
- Our `orderData` now correctly encodes deposits for ERC-7683 intents.

### Root Cause

The public Across API documentation focuses on REST endpoints and doesn't document low-level contract ABI details. We discovered inconsistencies by analyzing their [frontend implementation](https://github.com/across-protocol/frontend/tree/master/api).

### Contract Evidence:

- [across-protocol/…/SpokePoolPeriphery.ts](https://github.com/across-protocol/frontend/blob/d44a6cee4510aa1c03abee4d6e186a1e660a1515/api/_typechain/SpokePoolPeriphery.sol/SpokePoolPeriphery.ts) shows `exclusivityParameter`
- [across-protocol/…/build-deposit-tx.ts](https://github.com/across-protocol/frontend/blob/d44a6cee4510aa1c03abee4d6e186a1e660a1515/api/build-deposit-tx.ts) line 107 calls `spokePool.depositV3()` with `exclusivityParameter`
- [across-protocol/…/_utils.ts](https://github.com/across-protocol/frontend/blob/d44a6cee4510aa1c03abee4d6e186a1e660a1515/api/swap/approval/_utils.ts) line 170-171 maps API's `exclusivityDeadline → contract's "exclusivityParameter”`

### Changes Made

1. **Fixed ABI Field Name**: `exclusivityPeriod` → `exclusivityParameter`
   - Contract expects `exclusivityParameter` ([evidence](https://github.com/across-protocol/frontend/blob/d44a6cee4510aa1c03abee4d6e186a1e660a1515/api/build-deposit-tx.ts#L107))
   - Maps to `quote.deposit.exclusivityDeadline` (despite confusing naming)

2. **Fixed Deposit Nonce**: Hardcoded `0` → `quote.deposit.quoteTimestamp`
   - Contract uses `quoteTimestamp` as unique deposit identifier ([evidence](https://github.com/across-protocol/frontend/blob/d44a6cee4510aa1c03abee4d6e186a1e660a1515/api/build-deposit-tx.ts#L105))

3. **Confirmed Address Padding**: Recipients padded to `bytes32` for ERC-7683 cross-chain compatibility
